questions.text:
Consider the following relational schema:
Employee (empId, empName, empDept )
Customer (custId,custName, salesRepId, rating)
SalesRepId is a foreign key referring to empId of the employee relation. Assume that each employee makes a sale to at least one customer. What does the following query return?
SELECT empName 
FROM employee E 
 WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT custId
FROM customer C
WHERE C. salesRepId = E. empId
AND C. rating < > 'GOOD')
questions.solution:
The subquery finds this employee's customers whose rating is not 'GOOD'. NOT EXISTS keeps the employee only if there are none.

Since every employee has at least one customer, this means all of the employee's customers are rated 'GOOD'.

Answer: Names of all the employees with all their customers having a 'GOOD' rating

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Names of all the employees with at least one of their customers having a 'GOOD' rating
Names of all the employees with at most one of their customers having a 'GOOD' rating.
Names of all the employees with none of their customers having a 'GOOD' rating.
Names of all the employees with all their customers having a 'GOOD' rating.

Consider the relational schema given below, where eId of the relation dependentis a foreign key referring to empId of the relation employee. Assume that every employee has at least one associated dependent in the dependent relation.

The above query evaluates to the set of empIds of employees whose age is greater than that of
questions.solution:
The join keeps employees who have some own dependent with age [latex]\ge[/latex] the employee's age (eId = empId).

Subtracting them from all employees leaves those whose age is greater than every one of their own dependents.

Answer: all of his/her dependents

all dependents

questions.text:
Consider the transactions T1, T2, and T3 and the schedules S1 and S2 given below.
T1 : r1(x); r1(Z) ; w1(x); w1(Z)
T2 : r2(x); r2(Z); w2(Z)
T3 : r3(x); r3(x); w3(Y)

S1: r1(x); r3(Y); r3(x); r2(Y); r2(Z); w3(Y); w2(Z); r1(Z); w1(x); w1(Z)
S2: r1(x); r3(Y); r2(Y); r3(x); r1(Z); r2(Z); w3(Y); w1(x); w2(Z); w1(Z)
Which one of the following statements about the schedules is TRUE?
questions.solution:
S1: r2(Y) before w3(Y): T2[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T3; r3(x) before w1(x): T3[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T1; r2(Z), w2(Z) before r1(Z), w1(Z): T2[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T1. No cycle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] serializable (T2, T3, T1).

S2: r1(Z) before w2(Z): T1[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T2; r2(Z) before w1(Z): T2[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T1. Cycle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not serializable.

Answer: Only S1 is conflict-serializable

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Only S1 is conflict-serializable
Only S2 is conflict-serializable.
Both S1 and S2 are conflict-serializable
Neither S1 nor S2 is conflict-serializable

questions.text: What is the optimized version of the relation algebra expression  [latex]\pi _{A1}(\pi _{A2}(\sigma _{F1}(\sigma_{F2}(r))))[/latex] , where A1, A2 are sets of attributes in r with [latex]A_{1}\subset A_{2}[/latex] and F1, F2 are Boolean expressions based on the attributes in r?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Two selections combine: [latex]\sigma_{F1}(\sigma_{F2}(r))=\sigma_{F1\wedge F2}(r)[/latex]
- Since [latex]A_1\subset A_2[/latex], [latex]\pi_{A1}(\pi_{A2}(\cdot))=\pi_{A1}(\cdot)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\pi_{A1}(\sigma_{F1\wedge F2}(r))[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: [latex]\pi _{A1}(\sigma_{(F1 \wedge F2)}(r))[/latex]
[latex]\pi _{A1}(\sigma_{(F1\vee F2)}(r))[/latex]
[latex]\pi _{A2}(\sigma_{(F1\wedge F2)}(r))[/latex]
[latex]\pi _{A2}(\sigma_{(F1 \vee F2)}(r))[/latex]
